decision.justification: Two independent views of this merchant disagree with its declaration. The storefront presents a different business, and the the merchant's own statement channel agrees. Neither could have produced the other: a merchant cannot change its payment behaviour without changing its actual business, and cannot change its interface without changing what customers see.
notes: The corroborating view is the merchant's own account of itself. It was asked a neutral question about what it sells and described a different business from the one it declared.

attribution.label: Volume trend slope (vs category)
attribution.explains: Fitted daily growth rate of transaction count.

attribution.label: Round-value share drift (vs category)
attribution.explains: Recent minus prior window. Separates a merchant that has always priced in round numbers from one that started last month.

attribution.label: Round-value share (last 30d) (vs category)
attribution.explains: The same measure over the last 30 days only.

attribution.label: Post-peak persistence (vs category)
attribution.explains: Volume after the peak divided by volume before it. Near 1.0 means a spike that decayed -- a sale. Well above 1.0 means a step change that held.

attribution.label: Repeat-payer velocity (full window) (vs category)
attribution.explains: Transactions per unique payment instrument per day.

narrative.text: Merchant MID100035 declared apparel at onboarding 201 days ago. Telemetry agrees: the largest deviations from the apparel baseline are post_peak_persistence at +3.1 sigma (observed 1.4 against a category baseline of 1.05), round_share_drift at +3.0 sigma (observed 0.0503 against a category baseline of -0.00315), velocity_all at +2.6 sigma (observed 2.48 against a category baseline of 1.79). The checkout surface presents a crypto_exchange interface at 0.93 confidence, against a declared category of apparel. This vertical cannot be approved on this platform. Linked to 6 other merchants by rare shared asn, beneficiary id, device fp, ip block, payout fingerprint, phone fp, script bundle. Their payment behaviour is also moving in step (synchrony 0.52), which independent businesses do not do. It is linked to 6 other merchant accounts by rare shared asn, beneficiary id, device fp, ip block, payout fingerprint, phone fp, script bundle, and those accounts are moving in step (synchrony 0.52). Asked directly, the merchant described a crypto exchange business, which is not what it declared. In total 3 independent views of this merchant contradict its declaration. The investigation used 4 of a permitted 8 steps and stopped because confidence threshold met. Recommended tier restricts settlements, corroborated by the the merchant's own statement channel; the storefront alone would not have been sufficient.
